Wrought 625 samples were purchased from Rolled Alloys, Inc.

An EOSINT M290 (EOS GmbH, Munich, Germany) Directed Metal Laser Sintering (DMLS) machine equipped with a 400W Yb-fiber laser source was utilized to fabricate the additively manufactured (AM) Inconel 625 specimens.

An EOSINT M290 (EOS GmbH, Munich, Germany) Directed Metal Laser Sintering (DMLS) machine equipped with a 400W Yb-fiber laser source was utilized to fabricate the additively manufactured (AM) Inconel 625 specimens. Specimen fabrication was performed at the National Institution of Standard and Technologies (NIST).

12.5 mm × 12.5 mm × 102 mm coupons for creep tests were fabricated using DMLS process on a 250 mm × 250 mm substrate. The gas environment of the machine chamber was 99.995 % Ar and the oxygen level was maintained at less than 0.1 % O2. The substrate temperature was held at 80°C

The coupons were stress relieved at 800 °C for 1 hour after the DMLS fabrication process in the chamber of the EOSINT M290 machine. This heat treatment prevents warping of the samples.
the first heat treatment was solution annealing at 1100 °C for 1 hour in air
In the case of wrought samples, the same solution annealing heat treatment at 1100 °C for 1 hour in air was conducted before the creep tests.
5% volume fraction of MC carbides are present after solution annealing and are still observed after creep testing for 24 hours at both temperatures for the wrought alloy.
The MC carbide was not observed in the AM alloy, perhaps due to the low carbon concentration.
TEM found that there is 0.7 % γ” along with the initial MC carbides (5%) in the wrought alloy at 650 ˚C after 24 hours.
11% γ” was observed after 24 hours creep test in the AM alloy.
In the case of AM alloy after 24 hours creep test at 800 °C, no γ” was found, but, 11 % δ phase was observed.
